learningObjectives: Create and run unit test cases for Rules and Processes using assertions and test suites.
Use the Test Coverage tool to measure and analyze which Rules are covered by tests.

elements.text: Unit testing a Rule is like a quality inspector on a production line testing one specific component (a single bolt, a single circuit) with known inputs before it goes into the final product. The Test Pyramid is the assembly line strategy: test the cheap individual parts (unit tests) most often, and reserve expensive full-car crash tests (end-to-end) for last.

elements.description: Test individual Rules with defined inputs to isolate configuration errors. The earlier Unit tests v5 topic describes Actions > Run on a supported Rule form in Dev Studio; available interfaces depend on the Rule type.

elements.term: Binary file Rules — cannot be unit tested
elements.description: Unit tests v5 identifies binary file Rules as lacking a unit-test Run option. This is a version-scoped source detail, not a universal statement about every testing mechanism.

elements.term: Rule resolution applies during unit testing
elements.description: Normal Rule Resolution selects the applicable Rule in the test context. A higher version can run when eligible; version number alone does not override Ruleset availability, class and other resolution criteria.
A reusable test compares actual results with assertions. The current v6 examples include Property, Decision result, Expected run time and Page. Assertion availability depends on the Rule type.

Unit tests v5 describes sequential bulk suite execution and a Ruleset configured for test storage. This does not imply test dependencies: keep tests portable and independent. Configure execution through PegaUnit and run at least on each merge/check-in.
Test prioritization for Pega Unit Testing:
items: HIGH-PRIORITY — predictable results, executed frequently, complex logic, Rules with wide usage

LOW-PRIORITY automation examples: frequent maintenance, easy manual testing, complexity that resists automation, or database persistence. This is prioritization, not a reason to omit risk-based testing.

elements.caption: Rule execution and coverage roles are different concerns. Earlier v5 procedures are explicitly attributed.

elements.description: Convert a unit test run into a reusable test case. Define assertions (expected results). When the test case runs, results are compared to assertions — mismatch → test FAILS.

elements.term: Test cases for Processes and Case Types
elements.description: Actions → Record test Case (toolbar) → step through the flow entering input → click 'Create test Case' (lower-right) to save the recording. Modify pxCapturePropertyIgnore Data Transform to EXCLUDE unwanted properties from the test.

elements.term: v8.5+ restriction on Case Type test recording
elements.description: Creating unit test Cases v7 retains the 8.5+ restriction for running/recording a process with a Create Stage in a new Case Type. It describes an exception for migrated pre-8.5 Case Types; it does not guarantee all other recording prerequisites.

elements.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 760 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img" font-family="inherit"><title>Reusable tests and recording context</title><rect x="8" y="8" width="744" height="174" rx="12" fill="var(--pa-surface-2)" stroke="var(--pa-brand)"/><text x="28" y="40" fill="var(--pa-brand)" font-size="16" font-weight="700">Reusable tests and recording context</text><text x="28" y="78" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">Rule test: defined inputs → run → expected-result assertions → reusable test.</text><text x="28" y="110" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">Process recording: enter assignment/decision data; save the captured Data Transform.</text><text x="28" y="142" fill="var(--pa-ink-2)" font-size="14">Configure Setup & Cleanup; do not assume all source calls are automatically mocked.</text></svg>
elements.caption: Explicit setup, assertions and cleanup; a standalone assertion failure is not automatically a configured pipeline gate.

elements.description: Industry best practice for test strategy. Bottom of pyramid (unit tests): least expensive, easiest to maintain, fastest, should be the MOST tests. Top (end-to-end tests): most expensive, hardest to maintain, slowest, fewest tests. Higher up = higher cost.

Coverage reports identify executable Rules exercised or not exercised in included applications. Application-level reports combine multiple users; user-level results appear in Coverage history. A covered Rule is not proof that every internal path was tested.
Distinguish suite execution, coverage contribution and session initiation:
items: SysAdm4: role required by this topic to run test suites.
SysAdm4 or User4: tests can contribute to coverage.
pzStartOrStopMasterAppRuleCoverage: privilege required to initiate application-level coverage.
Application-level results: Application Quality Dashboard; user-level results: Coverage history. Merge application-level reports for consolidated results.

examPitfalls.title: Binary file Rules cannot be unit tested
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The earlier Unit tests v5 topic uses binary file Rules as an example without a Run option. Do not infer a complete unsupported-type list from that example.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check Rule-type support; the v5 source example has no unit-test Run option.

examPitfalls.title: Rule Resolution uses the eligible context, not version number alone
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A higher version that is not eligible in the application context does not automatically win.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Apply normal resolution; distinguish an opened Rule version from the Rule selected to execute.

examPitfalls.title: Sequential bulk suite behavior is the earlier v5 source workflow
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Do not turn this workflow into a guarantee about all possible external orchestration or introduce dependencies between tests.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The v5 topic describes sequential bulk execution; keep individual tests independent.

examPitfalls.title: Saving test cases requires a Ruleset configured to store them
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks why a unit test case cannot be saved. Candidates blame permissions. The actual requirement is a correctly configured Ruleset — without it the save operation fails regardless of user role.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: You cannot save test cases to a Ruleset not configured to store them. Work with the system administrator to identify the correct Ruleset before recording.

examPitfalls.title: v8.5+ restriction: no test recording for new Case Types with Create Stage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The v7 source retains a restriction on process recording for new Case Types with a Create Stage. It does not prescribe a universal manual-test workaround.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: From Pega v8.5+, recording a test case for a process with a Create Stage is NOT possible for NEW Case Types. Only works for Case Types migrated from versions lower than 8.5.

examPitfalls.title: User-level vs Application-level report visibility
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Coverage report scope differs from dashboard visibility: user-level reflects one contributor; application-level combines users.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: User-level: Coverage history. Application-level: Quality Dashboard, with authorized users contributing.

examPitfalls.title: Suite execution, coverage contribution and initiation have different requirements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: SysAdm4 for suite execution does not mean only SysAdm4 can contribute coverage or that this role alone initiates application-level coverage.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Contributors: SysAdm4 or User4. App-level initiator: pzStartOrStopMasterAppRuleCoverage privilege. Suite role: SysAdm4.

practiceQuiz.scenario: How do you run a unit test for a Rule in Dev Studio?

options.text: Click Actions → Run on the Rule form toolbar
Right-click the Rule in App Explorer and select Test
Navigate to Configure > Application > Quality > Test Coverage
Open the Rule and select PegaUnit from the header menu

practiceQuiz.hint: The Run option is on the Rule form toolbar.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Actions > Run is the procedure described in the earlier v5 topic.

optionExplanations.A: Actions > Run is the procedure described in the earlier v5 topic.
optionExplanations.B: The v5 topic does not describe this App Explorer action.
optionExplanations.C: Test Coverage reports execution coverage rather than invoking this Rule test.
optionExplanations.D: This header-menu procedure is not the one described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Rule test uses normal resolution. For the same eligible class and Ruleset, both v01.01.01 and v01.02.01 are available in the context, with no Branch or other overriding candidate. Which eligible version runs?

options.text: v01.02.01 — Rule resolution runs the higher version
v01.01.01 — the version that was opened runs
Both versions run and results are compared
The version in the current branch runs

practiceQuiz.hint: Pega applies normal rule resolution even when resolving rules during unit test execution.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The higher version wins among the eligible candidates as scoped here.

optionExplanations.A: The higher version wins among the eligible candidates as scoped here.
optionExplanations.B: Opening a lower version does not bypass normal resolution.
optionExplanations.C: The test does not automatically compare both Rule versions.
optionExplanations.D: This scenario explicitly excludes an overriding Branch candidate.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Rule type is the earlier Unit tests v5 topic’s example of a Rule without a unit-test Run option?

options.text: Binary file Rules
Decision Tables
When Rules
Data Transforms

practiceQuiz.hint: One Rule type has no Run option on its form.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Binary file Rules are the v5 example without the Run option.

optionExplanations.A: Binary file Rules are the v5 example without the Run option.
optionExplanations.B: Decision Tables are executable Rule examples for testing.
optionExplanations.C: When Rules are not the unsupported example identified here.
optionExplanations.D: Data Transforms are not the unsupported example identified here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the earlier Unit tests v5 workflow, how are suites executed when run in bulk?

options.text: Sequentially — one at a time in the specified order
In parallel — simultaneously for faster execution
In random order based on test priority
Only the first test suite runs; the rest are queued indefinitely

practiceQuiz.hint: Test suites in the Test Runner execute test cases one at a time sequentially.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The v5 topic describes sequential bulk suite execution.

optionExplanations.A: The v5 topic describes sequential bulk suite execution.
optionExplanations.B: Parallel bulk execution is not the behavior described in v5.
optionExplanations.C: The described execution is ordered, not random.
optionExplanations.D: The topic does not describe indefinite queuing after the first suite.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer wants to save a unit test case. What must be true about the target Ruleset?

options.text: The Ruleset must be configured to store test cases
The Ruleset must be the highest version in the system
The Ruleset must be locked for production
Any unlocked Ruleset can store test cases

practiceQuiz.hint: Use an accessible Ruleset configured to store test cases; being unlocked alone is insufficient.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The target Ruleset must be configured for storing test cases.

optionExplanations.A: The target Ruleset must be configured for storing test cases.
optionExplanations.B: Highest version alone does not enable test-case storage.
optionExplanations.C: A production lock does not supply the storage configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Unlocking alone does not enable the test-storage flag.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An assertion must verify that a specific page exists in memory after a Rule runs. Which assertion type is used?

options.text: Page — tests for the presence of a page in memory
Property — tests the value of a property
Decision result — tests a returned Decision Rule value
Run time — tests execution duration

practiceQuiz.hint: This assertion checks memory state, not property values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Page assertions address the page in memory.

optionExplanations.A: Page assertions address the page in memory.
optionExplanations.B: Property assertions compare a property value instead.
optionExplanations.C: Decision result assertions compare a Decision Rule result.
optionExplanations.D: Expected run time assertions compare execution duration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For a Process or Case Type eligible for recording, which workflow does Creating unit test Cases v7 describe?

options.text: Actions → Record test Case → step through → click 'Create test Case'
Actions → Run on the Rule form toolbar → convert to test case
Configure > Application > Quality > Test Coverage → Record
PegaUnit → New Case Type Test → step through flow

practiceQuiz.hint: Process/Case Type tests use recording, not the Run option.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This is the documented eligible Process recording workflow.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented eligible Process recording workflow.
optionExplanations.B: This describes individual Rule testing rather than the requested recording.
optionExplanations.C: Coverage reporting is not the recording workflow here.
optionExplanations.D: The source does not describe this New Case Type Test command.

practiceQuiz.scenario: From Pega Platform v8.5 onwards, when is it NOT possible to record a test case for a process?

options.text: When the process has a Create Stage in a new Case Type
When the process has more than 10 Stages
When the Case Type is in a locked Ruleset
When the process uses parallel processing

practiceQuiz.hint: This restriction applies to v8.5+, a specific Stage type, and new Case Types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source specifies this new-Case-Type/Create-Stage restriction.

optionExplanations.A: The source specifies this new-Case-Type/Create-Stage restriction.
optionExplanations.B: Ten Stages is not the stated version-specific restriction.
optionExplanations.C: Ruleset locking is not the particular restriction asked here.
optionExplanations.D: Parallel processing is not the restriction identified in the source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to the Test Pyramid, which test type is at the BOTTOM and should represent the MOST tests?

options.text: Unit tests
Integration tests
End-to-end tests
Performance tests

practiceQuiz.hint: Test pyramid: unit tests at the bottom — cheapest, fastest, and most numerous layer.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Unit tests form the broad, low-cost bottom layer.

optionExplanations.A: Unit tests form the broad, low-cost bottom layer.
optionExplanations.B: Integration tests are not the bottom layer requested.
optionExplanations.C: End-to-end tests occupy the expensive top layer.
optionExplanations.D: Performance testing is not the stated bottom layer.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which test coverage report aggregates results from multiple users and appears in the Application Quality Dashboard?

options.text: Application-level coverage report
User-level coverage report
Browser performance profile
PegaUnit coverage report

practiceQuiz.hint: One test coverage report type aggregates results from all users across the application.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Application-level reports combine multiple users’ coverage.

optionExplanations.A: Application-level reports combine multiple users’ coverage.
optionExplanations.B: User-level reports represent an individual contributor.
optionExplanations.C: A browser performance profile is not this coverage report.
optionExplanations.D: The requested source category is application-level, not this label.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which privilege does the source require to initiate application-level test coverage?

options.text: pzStartOrStopMasterAppRuleCoverage
The User4 role alone
Any developer role without the initiation privilege
Access to the Quality Settings page alone

practiceQuiz.hint: Initiating the application-level session is distinct from contributing coverage data.
practiceQuiz.rationale: This exact privilege is required to initiate app-level coverage.

optionExplanations.A: This exact privilege is required to initiate app-level coverage.
optionExplanations.B: User4 permits contributing coverage, not initiating an app-level session by itself.
optionExplanations.C: A developer role without the initiation privilege is not sufficient.
optionExplanations.D: Page access alone is not the initiation privilege named by the source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which role does a user need to run test suites in Pega Platform?

options.text: SysAdm4
SysAdmin
PegaDeveloper
TestManager

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish running a test suite from contributing coverage with User4.
practiceQuiz.rationale: SysAdm4 is the suite-execution role stated in this topic.

optionExplanations.A: SysAdm4 is the suite-execution role stated in this topic.
optionExplanations.B: SysAdmin is not the exact role named in the topic.
optionExplanations.C: PegaDeveloper is not the named suite-execution role.
optionExplanations.D: TestManager is not the named suite-execution role.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO kinds of unit test cases can be grouped for Rule-level and eligible Process testing?

options.text: Unit test cases that validate the behavior of individual Rules such as Data Transforms
Unit test cases that validate Process (Flow) execution paths and outcomes
Load test scripts for simulating concurrent user performance
Standalone external load-generator scripts, without conversion to Pega unit test cases

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish unit test case artifacts from standalone external test scripts.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Rule unit test cases fit this grouping, including Data Transform tests. Eligible Process unit test cases fit this grouping.

optionExplanations.A: Rule unit test cases fit this grouping, including Data Transform tests.
optionExplanations.B: Eligible Process unit test cases fit this grouping.
optionExplanations.C: Standalone load scripts are not these unit test case artifacts.
optionExplanations.D: Unconverted external scripts are not Pega unit test case artifacts.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is reviewing test coverage for a Pega application before release. Which TWO statements correctly describe what the Test Coverage tool provides?

options.text: Test Coverage identifies which Rules have been exercised during unit test execution
Coverage identifies untested Rules that may need additional tests; a covered Rule does not prove every internal path was tested
Test Coverage automatically generates and applies fixes for Rules that fail assertions
Test Coverage measures response time and memory usage for each executed Rule

practiceQuiz.hint: Coverage reports show exercised Rules; execution alone does not prove exhaustive assertions or branch coverage.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Coverage records exercised executable Rules. Uncovered Rules indicate gaps; covered Rules do not establish exhaustive paths.

optionExplanations.B: Uncovered Rules indicate gaps; covered Rules do not establish exhaustive paths.
optionExplanations.C: Coverage does not automatically repair failing assertions.
optionExplanations.D: This is not the response-time and memory performance tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Data Transform test depends on input data and has an expected result to verify. Which TWO elements make this test meaningful?

options.text: Input values that establish the data context the Rule will execute against
Assertions that define the expected output or property values after the Rule runs
A pipeline target environment where the test will be deployed and executed
A Report Definition to persist test execution results in the Pega database

practiceQuiz.hint: Every test case needs a known input and a defined expected output to verify correctness.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Define the input context required by this Data Transform. Assertions define the expected results to verify.

optionExplanations.A: Define the input context required by this Data Transform.
optionExplanations.B: Assertions define the expected results to verify.
optionExplanations.C: A pipeline target is not required for a standalone test’s input/result definition.
optionExplanations.D: A Report Definition is not required for this unit test configuration.

quickRecap.value: Earlier v5: Actions > Run; binary-file example lacks Run. Normal Rule Resolution applies to eligible context.
v6 examples: Property, Decision result, Expected run time, Page; available assertions vary by Rule type.
Earlier v5: sequential bulk suites and configured test Ruleset. The coverage topic states SysAdm4 for running suites.
Actions → Record test Case → step through → 'Create test Case'. v8.5+ restriction: no recording for Create Stage in NEW Case Types.
Bottom (unit tests) = cheapest/fastest/most. Top (end-to-end) = most expensive/slowest/fewest.
User-level: Coverage history. Application-level: multiple users, Quality Dashboard. Rule coverage is not exhaustive path coverage.
SysAdm4 runs suites; SysAdm4 or User4 contributes coverage; pzStartOrStopMasterAppRuleCoverage starts application-level coverage.
